sentences.text:
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.194/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Kalpetta, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166(1)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.12.2009.

According to the petitioner, on 29.12.2009 at about 10.30 p.m., while he was travelling in the autorickshaw bearing Reg.no.KL 10U/6021, a lorry bearing Reg.no.KL 07/AW 4432 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit against on the autorickshaw and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.9,61,000/- limited to Rs.5,00,000/-.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A20, X1 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,59,960/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Smt. Celine Joseph, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Smt.
K.S. Santhi, the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions 2025:KER:24769 MACA NO.1412 OF 2016 raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as a welder, earning Rs.11000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.7000/-.

The learned counsel for the insurer would argue Vineeth Kumar M vs The Managing Director on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51881818/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. It is true that the petitioner could not prove his income, as claimed in the OP.

According to him,
the petitioner was working as a welder, earning Rs.11000/- per month.
In order to substantiate the petitioner was examined his employer as PW1 and produced Ext.A10 salary certificate.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2009 will come to Rs.7000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner being a welder by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.8000/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.

12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
 Head injury  Bleeding from nose and ear.

2025:KER:24769 MACA NO.1412 OF 2016  Comminuted depressed frontal bone fracture  Contusion left frontal region  Laceration upper lip and forehead  Exposing skull bones with depressed fracture.
13. Ext. C1(a) disability certificate shows that the petitioner suffered 65.5% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 65%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.

The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.
I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 65.5%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 28 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in 2025:KER:24769 MACA NO.1412 OF 2016 Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.1496544/-.
15. Towards 'loss of earning', the tribunal has not awarded any amount.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 12 months.
Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.96000/- (8000 x 12 months).
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50000/-
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.50000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2500/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.

sentences.text: The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 76 days in 3 sessions.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.150000/-, Rs. 150000/- and Rs.10000/-
respectively.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.19,31,804/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
Sl.

Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in  Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal (in Rs.)

1 Loss of earning Nil 96000  2 Medical expense 12510 12510  3 Bystander expense 11400 11400  4 Transport to hospital 4350 4350  5 Extra nourishment 2500 10000  6 Damage to clothing 1000 1000  7 Pain and suffering 50000 150000  8 Compensation for permanent 928200 1496544  disability
9 Loss of amenities 50000 150000

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs. 19,31,804/- (Rupees Nineteen Lakhs Thirty One Thousand Eight Hundred and Four only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the 2025:KER:24769 MACA NO.1412 OF 2016 Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 138 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs,
within a period of two months from today.
(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%)
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
